question: Which facts must a GA agent handoff preserve for an integration decision, and what decision loss can a shared headline cause?
production_path: investigation: inspect the pinned GA Antigravity handoff bridge and its guaranteed fields
hypothesis: a shared ready headline cannot distinguish delivery states that require opposite decisions
test: four explicitly synthetic handoff cards with one headline, three boolean evidence gates, and asymmetric classroom costs
conclusion: measure toy decision loss and propose task-specific, checkable source and review references
hypothesis: If four distinct delivery states share the same ready headline but only one satisfies the toy integration rule, a headline-only receiver must make at least one wrong classification; retained gate evidence removes that ambiguity within the fixture.
evidence: At GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924, Scripts/antigravity-bridge.ps1 (Git blob cb4c999ebb615af327006045edb012c427c8858e) writes a handoff note with from, timestamp, branch, short head, dirty-line count, and caller-supplied free-form text. It does not execute or validate tests, review, or writer ownership.

The local teaching fixture state/streeling/fixtures/information-theory/inf-004/handoff-cases.json has four synthetic cases A-D all headed ready. Only A passes the three toy eligibility booleans; B, C, and D each fail one. This is not an observation of live GA handoffs.

Running evaluate_handoffs.py on the fixture yielded accept-all mean cost 7.5, reject-all mean cost 0.25, and full-evidence toy-rule mean cost 0 for invented false-accept cost 10 and false-reject cost 1. These numbers do not estimate production incident rates or actual financial loss.
No real agent handoff, merger, learner, human review, privacy-approved transcript sample, or public Learn page was evaluated. Duration was not instrumented, so duration_seconds=0.
